title: Hubble image of galaxy pair Arp 116
caption: The galaxy pair Arp 116, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Arp 116, M 60, Messier 60, NGC 4647, NGC 4649 · constellation Virgo · about 50 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image shows the peculiar galaxy pair Arp 116, made up of a giant elliptical galaxy, Messier 60, and a much smaller spiral, NGC 4647. They lie about 50 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo.

Astronomers have long debated whether the two are really interacting. They overlap as seen from Earth, but there is no sign of fresh star birth, and that would be among the clearest clues of an interaction. Recent studies of very detailed Hubble images, however, suggest that some tidal interaction may be beginning.

Just below and to the right of M60 sits an even smaller neighbor, M60-UCD1, only 1/500th the diameter of the Milky Way. It is densely packed, with about 140 million stars squeezed into just 300 light-years, and astronomers have found a supermassive black hole with the mass of 20 million Suns at its center.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.14 x 5.18 arcminutes) and distance (50 million light years), the frame spans roughly 89,000 × 75,000 light-years. Its light set out about 50 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's ACS and WFPC2 observed in blue, visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures and near-infrared light reveal detail beyond the reach of the eye.
